summary: Excellent node/edge editor with first-class React and provenance, but it is not a graph exploration engine: no built-in force or dagre layout, and you would add those yourself. Hold for this requirement; adopt it for workflow or editor UIs.
reasoning: MIT, SLSA provenance, 12.7M weekly downloads, 38.8k stars.
Small bundle for a React library: 58 KB gzip, 3 direct dependencies, 23 packages with React.
React >=17 peer range covers React 18 and 19.
It models nodes and edges on a canvas for editing, not graph analysis or automatic layout.
caveats: No built-in layout engine; pair with dagre/elk if automatic positioning is needed.
Not suited to force-directed exploration of Neo4j result graphs.
164 open issues, though the project is very active.

evidence.label: SLSA provenance
evidence.detail: Attestation present: builder github-hosted, source xyflow/xyflow, workflow .github/workflows/release.yml.

evidence.label: Dependency footprint
evidence.detail: 3 direct dependencies, 23 packages with React, 14.7 MB install, 58 KB gzip.

evidence.label: Fit for the requirement
evidence.detail: Node/edge editor, not a graph exploration or layout engine; layouts require dagre/elk.
